mainTopic: How שחיטה must be done: cuts in different places, the hidden knife (חלדה), and drawing the knife rather than chopping
overview: The גמרא first asks whether a שחיטה must be one clear cut in one place. רבי אבין answers his own challenge: a ברייתא that allows the סימנים to be cut at different heights means one slanted cut, like a reed pen. רבי זירא then learns from a story that our משנה allows two people with two knives to cut at different spots. Next, רב rules that hiding the knife between the סימנים (חלדה) makes the שחיטה invalid, even when the cut goes in the normal direction. A knife under the hide is valid, or, according to the school of רב, in doubt. Questions about a knife under a cloth, under tangled wool, or hidden for only a small part of the cut stay unresolved (תיקו). Then a new משנה teaches that two animals or two slaughterers are fine, but a single chop is invalid unless the knife slid across the neck. The גמרא proves from the 'drawn arrow' פסוק that שחיטה means drawing the knife. Finally, רבא slaughters a flying bird with an arrow, and the answer to whether that was חלדה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The worry that two slaughterers may press on each other
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the previous discussion. When two people slaughter together, one might cause the other to press the knife down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps each will cause the other to press the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last piece of the previous thought. It names the concern with two people slaughtering together: one may push the other into pressing the knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth is called דרסה, and it makes a שחיטה invalid. So when two people work together, there is a real practical risk to watch for.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps; a worry about what might happen
they will press the knife down (from דְּרָסָה), which makes the שחיטה invalid
one on the other; each causing the other

phrases.english: Perhaps each will cause the other to press the knife.
phrases.notes: Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it across ruins the שחיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an explanation that began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern with two slaughterers is that one may cause the other to press the knife (דרסה).

steps.title: רבי אבין asks about cutting the two סימנים at different heights
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין quotes a ברייתא that allows the gullet and windpipe to be cut at different heights on the neck. He asks how that can be, since the cut is then not one clear spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין objected from a ברייתא: if someone cut the gullet low and the windpipe high, or the gullet high and the windpipe low, the שחיטה is valid. But why? There is no clear, single-spot slaughter here!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין challenges the idea that שחיטה must be מפורעת, one clear cut in one place. He brings a ברייתא that seems to allow cuts in two different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sugya has been working with the idea that a valid שחיטה must be מפורעת, open and clear in one place. The ברייתא allows the וושט and the קנה to be cut at different heights. That looks like two separate cuts, so it seems to contradict that requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: the gullet (food pipe), one of the two סִימָנִים
the windpipe, the other סִימָן
below / above on the neck
a clear, open slaughter cut in one place
why? (here it introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin raises an objection:
If one cut the gullet below
and the windpipe above,
or the gullet above
and the windpipe below,
his slaughter is valid.
Why?
But there is no clear slaughter here!
phrases.notes: מפורעת means the cut is open and plain to see in one spot, not spread out across the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to the requirement of שחיטה מפורעת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement that שחיטה must be מפורעת, cut in one clear place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows the סימנים to be cut at different heights, which seems to show that a single-spot cut is not required.

steps.title: The ברייתא means one diagonal cut, like a reed pen
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין answers his own question: the ברייתא is talking about one slanted cut, shaped like the tip of a reed pen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he answered it: the case is a slaughter done like a reed pen.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין answers his own question. The ברייתא does not mean two separate cuts. It means one continuous slanted cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slanted cut starts high on one סימן and slides down, so it reaches the second סימן lower on the neck. It is still one continuous cut and still counts as מפורעת. So the requirement stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection
resolves, answers
a reed pen, whose tip is cut on a slant

steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the rule of שחיטה מפורעת standing. It also shows that a slanted cut is fine as long as it is one continuous cut.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ, וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raises the objection, and he resolves it:
It refers to a slaughter done like a reed pen.
phrases.notes: Picture the slanted tip of a reed pen. It is one cut that runs downward on a diagonal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ, וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow two separate cuts at different heights.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about one continuous diagonal cut, which is still מפורעת.

steps.title: A bull cut in several places, and a sage takes the best meat
steps.stepSummary: A bull was slaughtered with cuts in two or three places. רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא took its choicest meat, which shows he held it kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a bull that was slaughtered in two or three places. רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא went in and took meat from the very best parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case. It sets up the lesson רבי זירא draws in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the choicest meat shows that רב יצחק held this שחיטה fully kosher, even though the cuts were in several places. That seems to go against needing one single-spot cut.

keyTerms.meaning: a bull, an ox
was slaughtered
took
the very best parts

phrases.english: There was a certain bull that was slaughtered
in two or three places;

phrases.aramaic: עָל רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta went in
and took from the very best parts.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא תּוֹרָא דְּאִישְּׁחַט בִּשְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case about cuts in several places, the same topic as steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, an animal cut in two or three places was treated as kosher.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the משנה allows two knives and two people
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא learns from רב יצחק's action that our משנה, about two people slaughtering one above and one below, applies even with two knives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Our teacher, you have taught us that our משנה is talking even about two knives and two people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws a halachic lesson from what רב יצחק did. The משנה of two people slaughtering, one above and one below, includes two separate knives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two knives held by two people, each person cuts at a different spot on the neck. By eating from a bull cut in several places, רב יצחק showed he held this valid. So the משנה is not limited to two people holding one knife.

keyTerms.meaning: you have taught us
our teacher
our משנה
knives

steps.whatToRemember: רב יצחק's action, as רבי זירא reads it, shows that two people with two knives cutting at different spots still make a valid שחיטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It widens the משנה beyond one shared knife to separate cuts in different places.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
Our teacher, you have taught us that our משנה
is about two knives and two people.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about two people slaughtering one animal, one above and one below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: לִמַּדְתָּנוּ רַבֵּינוּ מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic lesson from the story in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה applies even to two knives and two people cutting at different places on the neck.

steps.title: Hiding the knife between the סימנים versus under the hide
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: hiding the knife between the two סימנים and cutting makes the שחיטה invalid, but hiding it under the hide is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If someone slipped the knife in between one סימן and the other and cut that way, the שחיטה is invalid. If he slipped it only under the hide, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רב about a slaughterer who hides the knife inside the neck while cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the knife must cut in the open, not while covered. If it is tucked between the windpipe and the gullet and cuts one of them from inside, the שחיטה fails. If only the hide (skin) covers the knife, רב says that does not ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: He hid or buried the knife, so it cut while covered (this is called חֲלָדָה)
One of the two signs that must be cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the gullet
Invalid (the שחיטה does not work)
Valid (the שחיטה works)
Under the hide, meaning the skin of the neck

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If one hid the knife
between one siman and the other siman
phrases.notes: He pushed the knife in between the windpipe and the gullet, then cut from there.

phrases.english: and cut it, it is invalid;
under the hide, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: חלדה, a hidden knife
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hiding the knife between the סימנים makes the שחיטה invalid; hiding it under the hide leaves it valid.

steps.title: Why does רב need to say this if a משנה already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's first ruling as unnecessary, since a משנה already says that hiding the knife under the second סימן invalidates the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב teaching us? We already learned in a משנה: if one hid the knife under the second סימן and cut it, רבי ישבב says it is a נבלה and רבי עקיבא says it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב said his first ruling at all, because a משנה already says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי ישבב and רבי עקיבא argue about how bad the animal is, either נבלה or טרפה. But both agree it may not be eaten. So hiding the knife already invalidates the שחיטה, and רב's ruling seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? The standard question when a statement seems to add nothing new
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה; it is forbidden to eat and also makes things טמא
An animal that is forbidden to eat but does not make things טמא the way a נבלה does

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישבב and רבי עקיבא are not arguing about whether the animal may be eaten. Both say it is forbidden. They only argue about whether it also carries the טומאה of a נבלה.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned this:
Or if one hid the knife
under the second one and cut it,
phrases.notes: He means the second סימן. He cut the first one normally, then cut the second from underneath.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yeshevav says: it is a neveila;
Rabbi Akiva says: it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of רב's ruling as unnecessary
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that hiding the knife between the סימנים is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already says that hiding the knife under the second סימן invalidates the animal, so רב's statement seems to repeat it.

steps.title: רב teaches that it is invalid even when cutting in the normal direction
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone we might have limited the rule to cutting upward. רב teaches that even cutting downward, the normal way, is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said it applies only when he cuts from below to above, since that is not the normal way of שחיטה. But when he cuts from above to below, the normal way, I would say it is fine. So רב teaches us that it is still invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing a case where we might have thought the hidden knife is fine. רב's ruling teaches that it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting upward, from under the סימן outward, is unusual, so we might have blamed the direction rather than the hiding. רב teaches that the hiding itself is the problem. Even when the cut goes in the normal downward direction, a hidden knife makes the שחיטה invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
From below to above, cutting upward
In the normal manner of slaughter
It is fine, it is allowed

steps.whatToRemember: חלדה (a hidden knife) invalidates שחיטה no matter which direction the cut goes. The problem is the hiding itself, not the direction.

phrases.english: If we had only the mishna, I would have said:
this applies only from below to above,
phrases.notes: He tucks the knife under the gullet and cuts outward, from the back of the neck toward the front.

phrases.english: because he is not doing it in the normal way of slaughter;
but from above to below,
since he is doing it in the normal way of slaughter,
I would say it is fine;
so he teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point: רב's ruling covers a case the משנה could have been read to leave out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hiding the knife is invalid only when cutting upward, against the normal way of שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: Hiding the knife is invalid even when cutting downward in the normal way

steps.title: Another version: רב was unsure about the knife under the hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the second half of רב's ruling. The school of רב reports that רב said he did not know the law when the knife is hidden under the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'under the hide, it is valid': the school of רב say that רב actually said, 'Under the hide, I do not know.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of רב's ruling and brings a different report of what רב said about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reported that רב called the case under the hide כשרה. The school of רב remember רב saying he was unsure. The doubt is whether skin covering the knife counts as hiding it, like the case between the סימנים, or does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The school, or students, of רב
I do not know, meaning the law is left in doubt

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reports of רב's view about a knife hidden under the hide: valid (רב יהודה), or unsure (the school of רב).

phrases.english: Under the hide, it is valid:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the second half of רב's ruling from step 6 so it can discuss it.

phrases.english: The school of Rav say:
Under the hide, I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the second half of step 6 and brings a different version of רב's words
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the school of רב, רב was unsure whether hiding the knife under the hide invalidates the שחיטה.

steps.title: Hiding the knife under a cloth or tangled wool
steps.stepSummary: רב said he did not know the law for a knife hidden under the hide. Building on that, the גמרא asks about a knife hidden under a cloth or under tangled wool. Both questions stay unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages asked: according to the school of רב, who say 'under the hide, I don't know,' what is the law if the knife was hidden under a cloth? What if it was hidden under tangled wool? These questions stay unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes רב's uncertainty about the hide and asks about two similar cases: a cloth wrapped around the neck, and thick tangled wool. It cannot decide either one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The school of רב were unsure whether a knife covered by the hide counts as hidden. The גמרא asks whether other coverings, a cloth or tangled wool, raise the same doubt. It finds no answer, so both questions end in תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the Sages, often one with no clear answer
A cloth or rag (here, one wrapped around the animal's neck)
Tangled, matted wool on a sheep's neck
'Let it stand.' The question is left unresolved

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
According to the school of Rav, who say:
"Beneath the hide, I do not know,"
phrases.notes: This is רב's uncertainty from the previous step, about a knife hidden under the animal's skin.

phrases.english: if it was beneath a cloth, what is the law?
If it was beneath tangled wool, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לְבֵי רַב, דְּאָמְרִי: תַּחַת הָעוֹר אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב's uncertainty about the hide to other coverings
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a knife hidden under a cloth or tangled wool count as חלדה?

steps.title: Hiding the knife for only a small part of the cut
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks what happens if the knife was hidden only while cutting a small part of the סימנים, and the larger part was cut normally. The question stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: if someone hid the knife while cutting the smaller part of the סימנים, what is the law? Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a new question about חלדה. What if only a minority of the cut was done with the knife hidden? The גמרא leaves it unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that hiding the knife during the whole cut makes the שחיטה invalid. A kosher שחיטה requires cutting only the majority of the סימנים. So the question is whether a problem in the extra minority still ruins it.

keyTerms.meaning: He hid or buried the knife inside the neck while cutting (חלדה)
The minority, meaning the smaller part, of the windpipe and food pipe
He asks, raises a question

steps.whatToRemember: Both questions about חלדה, the covered knife and the partial hiding, end in תיקו. They stay unresolved.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raises a dilemma:
If one hid the knife while cutting the minority of the simanim, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: הֶחְלִיד בְּמִיעוּט סִימָנִים מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further question about חלדה, now about a partial hiding
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does hiding the knife during only the minority of the cut invalidate the שחיטה?

steps.title: משנה: two heads at once, and two people slaughtering together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that slaughtering two animals at the same time is valid. Two people holding knives and slaughtering one animal is also valid, even if one cuts higher and one cuts lower.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who slaughters two heads at once has a valid שחיטה. If two people hold a knife and slaughter, even one above and one below, the שחיטה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A משנה is presented. It opens with two cases that might seem strange but are valid: one person slaughtering two animals together, and two people slaughtering one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that שחיטה does not have to be one person cutting one animal. Two cuts at different spots on the neck still combine into one valid שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the text the גמרא discusses
Two heads at once, meaning two animals slaughtered at the same time
Holding or grasping
Above and below, meaning at different points along the neck

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters two heads simultaneously,
his slaughter is valid.
If two people are grasping a knife and slaughtering,
even one above and one below,
phrases.notes: As step 5 showed, this applies even when each person has his own knife.

phrases.english: their slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה section begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering two animals at once, or two people slaughtering one animal, is valid.

steps.title: משנה: cutting off the head in one stroke
steps.stepSummary: Chopping off the head in one stroke is invalid. But if the person was slaughtering and the head came off in one stroke, it is valid if the knife is as long as the neck is wide. For two heads, the knife must be as long as one neck is wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut off the head in one stroke, it is invalid. If he was slaughtering and cut off the head in one stroke, it is valid if the knife is as long as a full neck. If he was slaughtering and cut off two heads in one stroke, it is valid if the knife is as long as one full neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now deals with cutting off the head in a single motion. It explains when that is invalid and when it is still a kosher שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single chop cuts without drawing the knife along the neck, so it is פסולה. If he was slicing with a knife at least as long as the neck is wide, the knife was drawn across the neck, so it counts as real slicing. With two animals, the knife only needs to be the length of one neck.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut off completely, severed (the head)
In one stroke, all at once
The full width of the neck, as a measure of the knife's length
Invalid (the animal is not kosher)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cutting off the head' is not automatically a problem. The issue is a single chop without slicing. When he was slicing with a long enough knife, the שחיטה is כשרה.

phrases.aramaic: הִתִּיז אֶת הָרֹאשׁ בְּבַת אַחַת – פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: If one cut off the head in one stroke, it is not valid.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה שׁוֹחֵט וְהִתִּיז אֶת הָרֹאשׁ בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: If he was slaughtering and cut off the head in one stroke,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בַּסַּכִּין מְלֹא צַוָּאר – כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: if the knife is the length of the full neck, it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה שׁוֹחֵט וְהִתִּיז שְׁנֵי רָאשִׁין בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: If he was slaughtering and cut off two heads in one stroke,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בַּסַּכִּין מְלֹא צַוָּאר אֶחָד – כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: if the knife is the length of one full neck, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתִּיז אֶת הָרֹאשׁ בְּבַת אַחַת פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the case of cutting off the head
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single chop is invalid. Cutting off the head while slaughtering is valid if the knife is at least the width of one neck.

steps.title: משנה: knife length only matters for a one-way cut
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the knife-length rule. It only applies when the knife moved in one direction. If he moved it back and forth, any knife is fine, even a tiny scalpel.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When he moved the knife forward and not back, or back and not forward. But if he moved it forward and back, a knife of any size works, even a scalpel. It is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by explaining when the 'full neck' length rule applies. It only matters for a single one-direction stroke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the length rule is to make sure the knife sliced across the neck. If the knife went back and forth, slicing already happened, so the size of the knife does not matter at all.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? A phrase that introduces a limit on the rule just stated
Moved the knife forward and back
Any amount, any size at all
A scalpel, a very small blade

steps.whatToRemember: What makes שחיטה valid is a slicing motion. A long knife is needed only for a one-way stroke. Back-and-forth slicing works with any blade.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic definition of how שחיטה must be done: by slicing, not chopping. The length of the knife matters only when that slicing would otherwise be in doubt.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
phrases.notes: He means the rule about the knife being the length of a neck.

phrases.english: When he moved it forward and did not bring it back,
or brought it back and did not move it forward;
but if he moved it forward and back,
even if the knife is of any size,
even with a scalpel, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוֹלִיךְ וְלֹא הֵבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the knife-length rule of the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The knife-length requirement applies only to a one-direction stroke. With back-and-forth motion, any blade is valid.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the drawing rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that chopping off the head in one stroke is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for the source of the rule that cutting off the head in one stroke is not valid. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a single chop is not valid, but a slaughter where the knife moves along the neck is valid. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that שחיטה requires a drawing motion.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? A request for a source
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's rule that chopping off the head in one stroke is not valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule from the משנה in Step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that שחיטה must be done by drawing the knife

steps.title: שמואל: the 'drawn' arrow
steps.stepSummary: שמואל brings a פסוק that calls an arrow 'שחוט', which teaches that שחיטה means drawing.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The פסוק says, 'Their tongue is a drawn (שחוט) arrow, it speaks deceit.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers with a פסוק from ירמיהו that uses the word 'שחוט' for an arrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An arrow flies because the bowstring is pulled back, so the word 'שחוט' carries the idea of drawing or pulling. Since the same root is used for שחיטה, slaughter must be done by drawing the knife across the neck, not by striking.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק
A 'drawn' arrow, shot by pulling the bowstring
Kosher slaughter

phrases.english: Shmuel said: As the verse states:
"Their tongue is a drawn arrow,
it speaks deceit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word שחוט describes a drawn arrow, so שחיטה means drawing the knife

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: וְשָׁחַט means drawing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that 'וְשָׁחַט' means drawing, and proves it from two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And he shall slaughter' (וְשָׁחַט) means nothing other than 'and he shall draw.' And so it says, 'drawn (שחוט) gold,' and it also says, 'Their tongue is a drawn arrow, it speaks deceit.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא backs up שמואל's idea. It says the word וְשָׁחַט in the תורה means drawing, and brings two פסוקים as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first cites 'זהב שחוט' from the story of שלמה's gold shields, and then the same arrow פסוק that שמואל used. Both show that the root שחט carries the idea of drawing or stretching.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall slaughter (ויקרא 1:5)
And he shall draw or pull
Drawn gold, gold that was stretched out or beaten
And it also says: brings a second פסוק

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And he shall slaughter": "and he shall slaughter" means nothing but "and he shall draw,"
and so it says: "drawn gold,"
and it says: "Their tongue is a drawn arrow, it speaks deceit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting שמואל's reading
steps.raayaObject: That שחיטה means drawing the knife
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל citing זהב שחוט and חץ שחוט

steps.title: Why a second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to add the second פסוק with 'and it says'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא was not satisfied with 'drawn gold' and added the arrow פסוק. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one proof is enough. When a ברייתא adds a second פסוק, the גמרא assumes the first proof had a weak spot and asks what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the point of "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the structure of the ברייתא in Step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first פסוק (זהב שחוט) was not enough

steps.title: 'Drawn gold' might mean thread-like gold
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק could be read as gold spun like thread, so the arrow פסוק is needed to prove the meaning of drawing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you would say that 'זהב שחוט' means gold that was spun like a thread (כחוט), come and hear: 'Their tongue is a drawn arrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'שחוט' in the gold פסוק might come from the word 'חוט' (thread), not from drawing. So the arrow פסוק is added, since there it must mean drawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could read שחוט as 'ש-כחוט', meaning 'like a thread', which would teach nothing about שחיטה. An arrow is not a thread, so in the arrow פסוק שחוט can only mean 'drawn', and that closes the gap.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: brings up a possible objection
Spun, like thread
Like a thread

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether gold can be spun. It is about the word: שחוט might be read as 'like a thread' (כחוט), which has nothing to do with drawing.
steps.whatToRemember: שחיטה must be done by drawing the knife. The proof is the 'drawn arrow' פסוק, because 'drawn gold' alone could mean 'thread-like gold'.

phrases.english: And if you would say that "drawn gold"
means it was spun like a thread,
phrases.notes: The word שחוט can be split as 'ש-כחוט', meaning 'that is like a thread'.

phrases.english: come and hear: "Their tongue is a drawn arrow."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא ״זָהָב שָׁחוּט״ שֶׁנִּטְוֶוה כְּחוּט הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Drawn gold' could mean thread-like gold, so the arrow פסוק is needed to prove the meaning of drawing

steps.title: רבא slaughters a flying bird with an arrow
steps.stepSummary: רבא checked an arrow for רבי יונה בר תחליפא and slaughtered a bird with it while it was flying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא checked an arrow for רבי יונה בר תחליפא, and slaughtered a bird with it while it was flying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: רבא made sure an arrow had no nicks and then used it to slaughter a bird in mid-flight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story ties into the arrow פסוק. It shows that a sharp, checked arrow that cuts by sliding across the neck can count as a valid שחיטה, even without a person holding the blade.

keyTerms.meaning: Checked the blade for nicks
An arrow
A bird
Flew

phrases.english: Rava examined an arrow
for Rabbi Yona bar Taḥlifa,
and he slaughtered a bird with it while it was flying.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא הֲוָה בָּדֵיק לֵיהּ גִּירָא לְרַבִּי יוֹנָה בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story connected to the arrow theme of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird slaughtered in flight by a checked arrow was treated as validly slaughtered

steps.title: Maybe the arrow made a hidden cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the arrow might have cut while hidden inside the neck, which is חלדה and not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it did חלדה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's story: perhaps the arrow went into the neck and cut the סימנים while hidden, which would make it not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב ruled that hiding the knife inside the neck while cutting (חלדה) makes the שחיטה invalid (steps 6-8). An arrow flying into a bird's neck could easily push inside before cutting, so the גמרא asks how רבא could rely on this.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Cutting with the blade hidden inside the neck; invalidates שחיטה

phrases.english: But perhaps it performed ḥalada?
phrases.notes: He means the arrow may have gone into the neck and cut while hidden, like the hidden-knife cases from before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the validity of רבא's arrow slaughter
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's slaughter of the flying bird with an arrow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An arrow may enter the neck and cut while hidden (חלדה), which invalidates שחיטה

steps.title: Start of the answer: we see
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with 'we see'; the rest continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the חלדה challenge by saying 'we see'. The answer only begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חזינן' shows the answer will rely on something that can be seen and checked. The details of what we see come next.

keyTerms.meaning: We see; something that can be checked by looking

phrases.english: We see

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical check: looking at the result
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The arrow may have cut while hidden (חלדה)
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is completed on the next amud
